# JSON-RPC method reference

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_rpc_docs.py from server.py. Don't edit by hand: run `make rpc-docs`. -->

Protocol, errors, CSRF, cookies and examples: [README.md](README.md).

54 methods: 7 public, 3 account, 5 market data, 30 user, 9 admin.

## Tiers

| Tier | Who may call | Handler |
|---|---|---|
| Public | anyone, signed in or not | gets the request context |
| Account | signed in | gets the request context |
| Market data | signed in; the same answer for every user | gets the params only |
| User | signed in; acts on the caller's own data | gets the caller's `user_id` first |
| Admin | signed in, with the role feature listed in REQUIRES | gets the request context |

## Parameter rules

`rpc_guard.validate` checks every call before it reaches the handler:

- `params` must be an object. Unknown names, missing required ones and wrong basic types are refused (error -32602).
- Numbers must be finite (no NaN or Infinity).
- Strings are at most 1000 characters.
- `symbol` is an NSE ticker in the current Nifty 50, except where a method notes otherwise.
- `expiry` is `YYYY-MM-DD`; `run_at` is `HH:MM`.
- `legs` is a list of 1 to 4 objects: `side` (`CE`/`PE`) and `strike` (> 0); order legs add `action` (`BUY`/`SELL`), `lots` (1 to 500) and an optional limit `price`.
- `lots` is 1 to 500; `limit` is 1 to 500; `price` is above 0.

## Limits

Named in the method descriptions below.

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `FORCE_SCREEN_EVERY` | 120 | seconds between forced screen refreshes, shared by all users |
| `DETAIL_EVAL_EVERY` | 15 | seconds between on-demand evaluations of one unscreened stock |
| `REPRICE_EVERY` | 30 | seconds between forced re-pricings, per user |
| `SESSION_DAYS` | 7 | days a session lasts without use |
| `SESSION_CAP_DAYS` | 30 | days a session lasts at most |
| `FAIL_WINDOW` | 900 | seconds over which failed sign-ins are counted |
| `FAILS_PER_PAIR` | 5 | failed sign-ins per email and IP in that window |
| `FAILS_PER_IP` | 30 | failed sign-ins per IP in that window |
| `SIGNUPS_PER_IP` | 5 | sign-ups per IP per hour |
| `CODE_TTL` | 600 | seconds a sign-up code is valid |
| `CODE_TRIES` | 5 | wrong guesses per sign-up code |
| `VERIFY_PER_IP` | 30 | code checks per IP in 15 minutes |
| `RESEND_GAP` | 60 | seconds between sign-up codes for one account |
| `CODES_PER_IP` | 10 | sign-up codes sent per IP per hour |
| `CODES_PER_DAY` | 5 | sign-up codes per account per 24 hours |
| `CONFIRM_DAYS` | 14 | days to confirm the email before the sign-up is blocked |
| `RESET_TTL` | 86400 | seconds a password-reset link is valid |
| `RESET_GAP` | 60 | seconds between reset emails for one account |
| `RESET_PER_IP` | 10 | reset requests per IP per hour |

## Public methods

Callable by: anyone, signed in or not.

### `auth_register`

Requests an account and emails a 6-digit code to confirm the address; once confirmed, the
account waits for admin approval. At most SIGNUPS_PER_IP sign-ups per hour from one IP.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `name` | `str` | required |
| `email` | `str` | required |
| `password` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `auth_login`

Signs in and sets the session cookie, with a new token every time. An unconfirmed account gets
error -32005 and a fresh code. Wrong passwords are limited per email and IP (FAILS_PER_PAIR) and
per IP (FAILS_PER_IP) within FAIL_WINDOW.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `str` | required |
| `password` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `auth_me`

The signed-in user with their saved theme and palette, or null when signed out.

Works while the account has a temporary password.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `auth_verify_email`

Confirms the sign-up email with the emailed code (spaces are ignored). CODE_TRIES guesses per
code and VERIFY_PER_IP checks per IP in 15 minutes. An unknown email gets the same answer as a wrong code.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `str` | required |
| `code` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `auth_resend_code`

Emails a new sign-up code: at most one per RESEND_GAP and CODES_PER_DAY a day. The answer is
the same for an unknown email.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `auth_forgot_password`

Emails a password-reset link valid for RESET_TTL. The answer is the same whether or not the
email has an active account. One email per RESET_GAP per account, RESET_PER_IP requests per hour per IP.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `auth_reset_password`

Sets a new password from the emailed reset token. The token works once, and every session of
the account is ended.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `token` | `str` | required |
| `new_password` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

## Market data methods

Callable by: signed in; the same answer for every user.

### `get_screened_candidates`

Returns the cached screen instantly. Never waits on NSE: the refresher thread keeps it fresh.
force_refresh only asks for an early background refresh; the cached rows are still returned.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `force_refresh` | `bool` | `false` |

### `get_trade_detail`

One stock's full screen row for `expiry` (YYYY-MM-DD). Without it, or once that cycle has
rolled off the screen, the nearest cycle at least MIN_DTE days out.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |
| `expiry` | `str \| None` | `null` |

### `get_config`

The screening thresholds the UI shows (engine/config.py) and the current Nifty 50 list.

No params.

### `get_market_calendar`

NSE trading holidays and Nifty 50 corporate events, from the worker's daily copy, plus the
expiry dates the last screen covered (the calendar groups events by expiry cycle).

No params.

### `calc_margin`

SPAN + exposure for SHORT legs [{side, strike}] at `lots` lots, ignoring existing positions.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |
| `expiry` | `str` | required |
| `legs` | `list` | required |
| `lots` | `int` | `1` |

### `va_price_levels`

Price history and floor pivots for a stock the user holds (Portfolio chart). Limited to held
stocks so a client can't use it to make the server fetch arbitrary tickers.

`symbol` may be outside the Nifty 50: the method only acts on stocks the caller holds.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_cancel_order`

Cancels an open limit order, which releases its blocked margin. Refused once it has filled
or ended.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `order_id` | `int` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_modify_order`

Changes an open limit order's price. If the market already meets it, the order fills now at the bid/ask.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `order_id` | `int` | required |
| `price` | `float` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_preview_order`

Prices an order without placing it. legs: [{side, strike, action: 'BUY'|'SELL', lots, price?}].
`price` is the limit; without it it's a market order and the limit defaults to the touch price (the bid for a sell, the ask for
a buy) — gated by _check_liquidity so a thin quote can't book a bad fill. Returns each leg's
limit, whether it fills now, and the margin impact.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |
| `expiry` | `str` | required |
| `legs` | `list[dict]` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_place_order`

Places an order on the virtual account. Always prices fills itself from live quotes. While an
earlier order on the same stock and expiry is still waiting, it refuses unless `confirm_waiting` is set, so a
second click never doubles the trade by accident. A leg on an illiquid strike (wide spread, thin
OI, stale last trade) needs `confirm_illiquid`: the ticket shows why before asking.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |
| `expiry` | `str` | required |
| `legs` | `list[dict]` | required |
| `sl_mode` | `str \| None` | `null` |
| `confirm_waiting` | `bool` | `false` |
| `confirm_illiquid` | `bool` | `false` |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_exit_position`

Closes one open position with a limit at the touch. With the market shut, or no bid/ask, it
becomes an open limit order at the last price instead.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `position_id` | `int` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_exit_group`

Closes every open leg in one stock and expiry, the same way as exit_position. Works for a
stock that has since left the Nifty 50.

`symbol` may be outside the Nifty 50: the method only acts on stocks the caller holds.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |
| `expiry` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_set_sl_mode`

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `str` | required |
| `position_id` | `int \| None` | `null` |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_dismiss_alert`

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `position_id` | `int` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

|---|---|---|

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_get_autotrade`

The user's auto-trade settings, the next scheduled run, and whether a run is in progress.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_set_autotrade`

Changes auto-trade settings; an omitted field keeps its value. run_at is HH:MM from 09:15 to
15:29 IST, min_pop 50-99, reserve_pct 0-90, max_trade_pct 1-100. Returns the updated settings.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | `bool \| None` | `null` |
| `run_at` | `str \| None` | `null` |
| `min_pop` | `float \| None` | `null` |
| `reserve_pct` | `float \| None` | `null` |
| `max_trade_pct` | `float \| None` | `null` |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_autotrade_runs`

Past auto-trade runs, newest first, with what each placed.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `int` | `20` |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `va_autotrade_run_now`

Runs auto-trade on the current screen. Refuses while a screen is still in progress.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_connect_url`

Starts connecting the caller's Zerodha account: the Kite login URL and a one-time `state` to
pass back to broker_exchange_token. Needs the live_trading feature.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_exchange_token`

Finishes connecting Zerodha: swaps Kite's one-time request_token for an access token, stored
encrypted. `state` must be the one broker_connect_url returned. One active connection per user.
Needs the live_trading feature.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `request_token` | `str` | required |
| `state` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_status`

The user's latest broker connection: broker, status, broker user id, connection and token
expiry times. Never the tokens.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_disconnect`

Revokes the broker session and marks the connection disconnected.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_get_positions`

Real positions from the poller's last snapshot. Refused without an active connection.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_get_margins`

Real margins from the poller's last snapshot. Refused without an active connection.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_account_summary`

Unified real-or-approx shape for every place that shows margin figures for real trading:
the broker account page, the broker connect banner, and the order ticket's real-order side.
Real figures when an active, unexpired connection exists (reusing _require_active, so an
expired connection is flipped to 'expired' here the same as everywhere else that checks it);
otherwise the virtual account's own numbers stand in as an approximation, clearly flagged via
`source`. Both branches feed the same margin-shaped dict `m` into one return statement instead
of duplicating the 10-key result. The fallback reads the connection row off the _Inactive
exception rather than querying it again via status().

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_preview_order`

Prices every leg (all SELL) and checks the total margin required against the broker's own
real available funds — never against the virtual account. Returns a one-time confirm_token;
nothing is sent to the broker until broker_place_order redeems it.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `symbol` | `str` | required |
| `expiry` | `str` | required |
| `legs` | `list[dict]` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_place_order`

Places a previewed order on the real broker account; the only function that calls the
broker. Redeems a one-time preview; places every leg as a SELL LIMIT order sequentially. Kite Connect has no atomic multi-leg order: if a leg fails
after an earlier one already placed, this stops immediately and does not roll anything back —
an automatic square-off would itself be a new, unconfirmed real-money order.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `confirm_token` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

### `broker_stop_alerts`

Real legs and their broker-side stop, newest first, for the Broker account page.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `user_id`.

## Admin methods

Callable by: signed in, with the role feature listed in REQUIRES.

### `admin_list_users`

Every account past email confirmation, waiting requests first. Each lists the other accounts
that share its browser or network.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_set_status`

Approves (active), rejects or disables an account. Any status but active signs the user out
everywhere. Refused for the caller's own account.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `target_id` | `int` | required |
| `status` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_reset_password`

Issues a one-time temporary password, returned once. The user is signed out everywhere and
must set a new password on their next sign-in.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `target_id` | `int` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_audit_log`

The newest `limit` audit events (sign-ins, admin actions, broker events) with actor, target
account and IP.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | `int` | `100` |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_list_blocked`

Sign-ups not confirmed within CONFIRM_DAYS, newest first.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_unblock_signup`

Gives a blocked sign-up a fresh CONFIRM_DAYS and emails a new code. `sent` is false when the
email failed. The person still confirms the email, then waits for approval.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `target_id` | `int` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_set_role`

Changes an account's role to sub_admin, beta or user. Only the owner grants or removes
sub-admin; others move lower-ranked accounts between beta and user. Nobody can be made owner.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `target_id` | `int` | required |
| `role` | `str` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_get_features`

Owner only: which features each role (sub_admin, beta, user) has, and the feature list.

No params.

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.

### `admin_set_feature`

Owner only: turns one feature on or off for a role. Applies on the role's next request.

| Param | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `role` | `str` | required |
| `feature` | `str` | required |
| `enabled` | `bool` | required |

Set by the server, never by the client: `_ctx`.
